title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet courtyards, and high-vantage points that ASU students use to escape the bustle of the Tempe campus.

cards.title: The Secret Garden
cards.subtitle: Between Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall
cards.notes: Enter through the inconspicuous stairwells at Dixie Gammage Hall to find this sunken, grassy courtyard used for quiet reading and outdoor breaks.
cards.short_summary: A secluded, sunken courtyard hidden between historic campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Secret Garden is a beloved quiet spot hidden between Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall, often used by students for solitude.
cards.access_notes: Open public outdoor space; most quiet during evening hours.

cards.title: Luhrs Arizona Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Visit this first-floor room for a focused, silent environment surrounded by Arizona-themed collections and rotating cultural exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A silent reading room on the first floor of Hayden Library featuring Arizona collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Luhrs Arizona Reading Room on the first floor of Hayden Library offers a quiet space for focused studying and houses print collections pertaining to Arizona.
cards.source_title: First floor featured collections - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open during Hayden Library hours; typically 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Life Sciences Tower Lookout
cards.subtitle: Life Sciences Center, 7th Floor
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the top floor of the E Wing to access a quiet landing with expansive views of 'A' Mountain and the Tempe skyline.
cards.short_summary: A high-vantage point on the top floor of the Life Sciences Tower offering views of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The seventh floor of the Life Sciences Center (E Wing) provides a lookout point with views of Hayden Lawn and downtown Phoenix.
cards.source_title: The best places on ASU's Tempe campus to relax and unwind
cards.access_notes: Accessible via elevator in the E Wing during building hours.

cards.title: Student Services Courtyard
cards.subtitle: 1151 S. Forest Ave
cards.notes: Find the tables tucked along the sides of this grassy courtyard for a silent outdoor study spot away from the main campus thoroughfares.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, grassy outdoor courtyard adjacent to the Student Services Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The courtyard next to the Student Services Building is an underappreciated silent outdoor spot with tables and chairs.
cards.source_title: 5 hidden study spots on ASU's Tempe campus
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor area; accessible 24/7 but best during daylight.

cards.title: ISTB4 Third Floor Nooks
cards.subtitle: Interdisciplinary Science and Technology IV
cards.notes: Explore the third floor for secluded seating areas that offer a quieter environment than the more popular library hubs.
cards.short_summary: Secluded study seating located on the third floor of the ISTB4 research building.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of ISTB4 often provides a quiet environment with lots of seating and a more secluded feel than popular study spots.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Noble Library Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: 601 E. Tyler Mall
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for designated quiet zones and individual study rooms that are ideal for intense, distraction-free work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study area on the second floor of the Noble Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Noble Library has designated quiet zones on the second floor and more than 75 study rooms for individual or group use.
cards.source_title: Study rooms in Noble Library - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; check the ASU Library website for current daily schedules.

cards.title: Student Pavilion Lounges
cards.subtitle: 400 E. Orange Street
cards.notes: Use the open lounge spaces on the second floor for group collaboration or casual study in a modern, net-zero energy building.
cards.short_summary: Modern lounge and study spaces on the second floor of the Student Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Pavilion's second floor houses office space for student government and open areas suitable for student use.
cards.source_title: Student Pavilion - Educational Outreach and Student Services
cards.access_notes: General building hours are 7 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Monday through Friday.

cards.title: Design Library Silent Room
cards.subtitle: Design North Building, Level 1
cards.notes: Utilize one of the largest silent study rooms on campus, featuring individual carrels and large tables for spreading out projects.
cards.short_summary: A large, dedicated silent study room within the Design and the Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Design and the Arts Library boasts one of the largest silent study rooms with tables and individual study carrels.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open to ASU students and staff; visitors have limited hours.

cards.title: Music Library Quiet Nooks
cards.subtitle: Music Building, East Wing
cards.notes: Find near-silent study spots on the west side of the library, often less crowded than the main campus libraries.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study nooks located within the specialized Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library provides near-silent study on its west side with study nooks and tables.
cards.access_notes: Open during Music Library hours; typically 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Planetary Health Courtyard
cards.subtitle: University Dr & Rural Rd
cards.notes: Relax in the geode-inspired interior courtyard, designed with riparian features and cool blue-green walls to mimic a desert oasis.
cards.short_summary: A desert-inspired interior courtyard within the Walton Center for Planetary Health.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walton Center for Planetary Health features an interior courtyard modeled after a geode with a riparian area and light-filled spaces.
cards.source_title: The Rob and Melani Walton Center for Planetary Health at Arizona State University: Case Study
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; includes exhibit spaces.
